findings.detail: Every pre-attempt figure (22 in Core2A, 16 in Core2B) is emitted with the full representation markup. The later stages are only hidden by CSS display:none. The SVG's aria-labelledby points at <title> and a <desc> that narrates every stage, including the result. In Chromium the accessible name of the Q-PHY-NLM-2A-COV-05 pre-attempt image is 'Trolley with a 9 N pull … Stage 2: … a = +2 m/s². Stage 3: … a = −1.6 m/s²'. For Q-PHY-NLM-2B-FRICTION-STATE-01 it is '… Trial 2: N = 100 − 30 = 70 N, limit 38.5 N, need 40 N …', which is the protected move. A screen-reader learner therefore hears the answer before any attempt. The same text is inside article.textContent, so the page search also finds it. For a PRE_ATTEMPT mount, emit only the pre-attempt stage group and a description of that stage alone (e.g. 'A 2.5 kg trolley on a level track is pulled forward with 9 N while a 4 N drag acts backward'). Keep the full <desc> for the POST_ATTEMPT mount inside the gated disclosure.

Many representation <title>s state the answer or the protected move. The title is shown on the pre-attempt figure as the SVG hover tooltip and as the image's accessible name. Core2B: FRICTION-ZERO-03 'Crate in a lift accelerating up: N = 600 N, friction zero'; FRAME-SELECTION-05 '… rest in the car frame with a 1.5 N pseudo-force'; FRICTION-WALKING-02 '… friction forward on the shoes, backward on the plank'; CONSTRAINT-VS-TENSION-07 'Heavy pulley: the length relation holds, one tension does not'; CONTACT-LOSS-06 '… keep the contact model only while N ≥ 0'; STRING-MODEL-03 '… tension grows toward the top'; INCLINE-2B-FRICTION-DIRECTION-02 '… friction up, zero, then down'; ANGLED-THRESHOLD-04 '… a steep enough push can never start the block'. Core2A: COV-04 '… static friction backward, 20 × 3 = 60 N'; FRICTION-ZERO-08 '… friction is zero'; FRICTION-STATIC-09 '… actual 12 N, limit 30 N'; FRICTION-KINETIC-10 '… kinetic friction 10 N'; ATWOOD-12 '… T lies between the two weights'; INCLINE-2A-SMOOTH-01 '… N = mg cos θ, a = g sin θ'; INCLINE-2A-STATIC-02 '… rest needs mg sin θ ≤ μ_s mg cos θ'; INCLINE-2A-SLIDING-03 '… a = g(sin θ − μ_k cos θ)'; FIXED-PULLEY-04 '… y_A + y_B = constant'. Give each representation a situation-only title for pre-attempt use (e.g. 'A 50 kg crate on the rough floor of a lift accelerating upward'). The result-bearing title can stay on the post-attempt mount.

The Core1B tasks are new, but the rest of each unit still describes the old Core1A scenario, so the reconstruction does not rebuild the task the learner attempted. 'Your answer should contain' (elicitation.attempt.produces) does not match the task in: NET-ZERO-MOTION (car at 25 m/s vs 'a two-case prediction for a released moving cart and an initially resting cart'); FBD-BODY-OWNERSHIP (man in a boat vs 'two separate body inventories, one for the cart and one for the horse'); FRAME-CHOICE (braking train vs 'roadside and accelerating bus'). The reconstruct prompts ask about the hand leaving the cart (NET-ZERO), two people pushing a box (FORCES-SUM-ZERO), horse and cart (FBD), the bus starting (FRAME-CHOICE) and 'the box's ground-frame velocity' (FRICTION; the task is a block pressed on a wall). Rewrite the rubric line and the reconstruct prompts for the actual task. For example, for FBD: 'Which body is the diagram for? Which forces act on the boat: Earth, man, water? Is the man's weight on the boat's diagram? What must the water's push be for the boat to stay at rest?'

Each of the 11 Core1B units mounts its Core1A worked-anchor figure, pre-attempt and post-attempt, not a figure of the Core1B attempt. For FRICTION-QUANT the attempt is a 5 kg box with a 30 N push, then a 20 N press (N = 50 N slides; N = 70 N rests). The figure shows '4 kg box pulled with 15 N and 25 N'. For SECOND-LAW the attempt is a 1200 kg car braking under 5400 N + 600 N, and the figure is the 10 kg crate on a 30° ramp. For THIRD-LAW the attempt is a 400 kg rocket and 5000 N of exhaust, and the figure is the astronaut and satellite. The post-attempt reconstruction figure shows the Core1A answer, not this attempt's. Each Core1B attempt needs its own figure: situation-only before the attempt, staged with this task's values afterwards.

transfer.novelty is not true against Core1B. Its checked_against list cites only the Core1B boundary test, not the Core1B FRICTION-QUANT attempt. That attempt already asks the learner to decide an unstated contact state with N changed by a vertical force, and it reaches opposite verdicts in two trials: 5 kg, 30 N push, N = 50 N, limit 25 N → slides, f_k = 20 N, a = 2 m/s²; add a 20 N press, N = 70 N, limit 35 N → rest, f = 30 N. Task 01 repeats that decision with the vertical force reversed: an angled pull lowers N to 70 N, limit 38.5 N < 40 N → slides. Either change the demand (for example, ask for the pull angle at which the verdict flips, or the smallest pull that starts the crate at 37°) or recheck the novelty claim against the Core1B attempt prompts.

Hint rung 4 of 5 gives the answer before the last rung: 'With N = mg cos θ and the needed friction mg sin θ up the slope, write the no-slip condition: mg sin θ ≤ μ_s mg cos θ.' That inequality is the answer's first form, and rung 5 only simplifies it. Rung 4 should stop at the relation to test ('compare the friction rest needs with the most the contact can give, μ_s N') and leave the inequality for the learner to write.

Still open from the previous review. Every page's h1, <title> and breadcrumb read 'Authored Grade-9 Force and Laws of Motion spine covering balanced/unbalanced for', which is scope_summary cut mid-word (the manifest title). Use a learner-facing title such as 'Force and laws of motion'.

Two Core2A items restate Core1A exit tasks whose model answers the learner has already opened. FRAME-CHOICE-07 (bus accelerating, loose object, roadside vs passenger, where the pseudo-force goes) is the FRAME-CHOICE exit task. Q-PHY-NLM-2A-FIXED-PULLEY-04 (y_A + y_B = constant, derive v and a relations) is the SINGLE-STRING-CONSTRAINT exit task, and its last part is the Core1 compact anchor (a_B = −a). Give each a new instance with values, e.g. a 0.5 kg box on a smooth shelf in a bus at 1.5 m/s² for 07.

Two Core1A units still have a figure that does not show their worked anchor. FBD-BODY-OWNERSHIP draws the qualitative horse and cart, but the anchor is a 50 kg child on a 20 kg box (200 N, 500 N, 700 N), which is never drawn. FRAME-CHOICE draws a qualitative lift 'v down, a up', but the anchor is a 60 kg person in a lift accelerating up at 2 m/s² with a 720 N reading in both frames. The physics in both figures is right; they just carry none of the anchor's values.

Inconsistent count. The figure title and stage 2 say the diagram 'counts gravity twice', the answer says it 'double-counts gravity', and the failure signal says the student's diagram 'counts gravity three times'. With mg, mg sin θ and mg cos θ drawn together, one force appears three times. Use one wording, e.g. 'the weight is drawn three times: once as mg and again as its two components'.

Still open. Option labels are doubled ('(a) (A) (F/2m)·a/sqrt(a^2-x^2) (b) (B) …') on every lettered or numbered source option (Q03, Q10, Q33, Q19, Q08, NEET Q160, Q49, Q40). Print the source label once.

Still open. Gating holds in Chromium: 0 of 84 gated disclosures across core1a, core1b, core2, core2a and core2b opened on click, Enter or Space without an attempt; an empty attempt did not unlock; hints reveal one rung per click (1 → 2 → 3, then 'Next hint' disabled); stage stepping, search filter and the display panel (theme, zoom) work. But any 3 characters ('abc') unlock a unit. The search filters on article.textContent, which includes locked answers and pre-attempt figure descriptions, so typing an answer value (e.g. '1.6') singles out the item that contains it. The wedge figure of Q-PHY-NLM-INCLINE-2B-COMPONENT-TRAP-04 also overprints 'block on wedge: 17.3 N' on the '5 kg' label.
